claims.text: Introducing 1–5 at.% uranium into an HEA superconductor alters local lattice strain around uranium sites.
Introducing 1–5 at.% uranium into an HEA superconductor alters local electron density around uranium sites.
Uranium atoms have an f-electron configuration relevant to their behavior in the proposed HEA.
Uranium dopants introduce localized electronic states in the HEA.
The uranium-induced localized states modulate the HEA electronic structure.
The uranium-induced localized states modify the local bonding environment in the HEA.
The uranium-induced changes in strain, electron density, electronic structure, and bonding enhance electron-pairing interactions.
Enhanced electron pairing caused by uranium doping increases the superconducting transition temperature.
Uranium-doped HEA samples will exhibit a statistically significant increase in Tc relative to an identically processed undoped baseline.
Low uranium concentrations of 1–5 at.% can be introduced while maintaining a homogeneous single-phase HEA.
The proposed mechanism is limited to uranium concentrations that preserve a homogeneous alloy phase.
The upper concentration for preserving a homogeneous phase is typically about 5 at.% uranium.
The proposed mechanism applies only to HEA systems in which electron-phonon coupling dominates superconductivity.

contradictions.description: The boundary restricts the hypothesis to homogeneous, single-phase samples, whereas the falsification rule treats observed phase separation or inhomogeneity as falsification. Phase separation would instead violate the stated boundary conditions and confound or invalidate the test, not decisively falsify the mechanism within its claimed domain.
